title: browsertrix: import a user's WACZ files from Browsertrix
description:
Add a 'rustyweb browsertrix' subcommand that authenticates to a Browsertrix instance (Webrecorder's hosted crawling service, which produces the WACZ files rustyweb serves), lists a user's archived items, downloads each WACZ into the home directory's archive folder, and indexes it as a local (File) source.

Grounded in the Browsertrix REST API (from its OpenAPI):
- Auth: POST /api/auth/jwt/login (form username/password) -> JWT bearer token.
- Whoami/orgs: GET /api/users/me, GET /api/orgs (paginated).
- List items: GET /api/orgs/{oid}/all-crawls (crawls + uploads), paginated.
- WACZ: GET /api/orgs/{oid}/all-crawls/{id}/download (authenticated stream) for downloading; GET /api/orgs/{oid}/crawls/{id}/replay.json for presigned resource URLs. Collections: /api/orgs/{oid}/collections/{id}/download.

DESIGN
- Command: rustyweb browsertrix [--host URL] [--org SLUG] [--home DIR] [filters].
- Uses --home like the other subcommands (default '.'); WACZs are written under <home>/archive and the index under <home>/index.
- Host default https://app.browsertrix.com; --host for self-hosted.
- Credentials from env (BROWSERTRIX_USER / BROWSERTRIX_PASSWORD) rather than flags, so passwords do not appear in the process list. (Optionally a token.)
- Flow: login -> resolve org (--org or the sole org) -> list all-crawls (paginated) -> for each item, download its WACZ into <home>/archive/<name>.wacz, then index that local file.
- ALWAYS DOWNLOAD (no --no-download for now): stream the authenticated /download endpoint straight into <home>/archive and index as a File source, so it is durable and replayable long-term. This matches rustyweb's rule that local WACZs live under <home>/archive (index stores them home-relative and portable). Browsertrix presigned/replay.json URLs are short-lived, so indexing them as remote URL sources would break replay after expiry - hence we download. (A remote/no-download mode was considered and deferred: rustyweb-15z.4, closed.)
- Provenance + incremental: record the Browsertrix item id on the collection so re-runs skip already-indexed items unless --force.
- Reuse ureq + serde_json; no new heavy deps. Test against a mock HTTP server serving canned JSON, not the live service.

This is a way to close the loop with Webrecorder, whose Browsertrix creates the WACZ files and whose ReplayWeb.page does the replay.
notes: When implemented, imported WACZs should be assigned to a Collection per the two-level model in rustyweb-collections-model-5co, and downloaded into <home>/archive (already reflected in this epics design).

Remaining follow-up split out: rustyweb-browsertrix-verify-download-hash-tmrn (verify download vs replay.json hash).

title: Verify downloaded WACZ against the Browsertrix replay.json hash
description:
The Browsertrix importer (rustyweb-15z.3) downloads each WACZ from its presigned replay.json URL but does not verify the bytes against the resource hash the API provides (replay.json resources[].hash, e.g. sha256:...). The .part→rename dance guards against a partial/truncated write, and indexing records its own SHA-256 (so `rustyweb verify` can detect later corruption) — but we do not catch a silently-wrong/corrupt download AT import time, against the source-of-truth hash.

Add: after download_wacz, compute the SHA-256 of the downloaded file and compare to res.hash (strip the "sha256:" prefix); on mismatch, delete the file and error out for that item (do not index). Reuse collections::file_sha256. Cheap (one pass over the just-written file) and turns a bad download into an immediate, clear failure instead of a subtly broken crawl.

Files: main.rs (download_wacz / run_browsertrix). Small; add a unit or e2e assertion (serve wrong bytes → import errors).

title: Import public Browsertrix collections (no login required)
description:
Let a curator import a PUBLIC Browsertrix collection — one Webrecorder (or a self-hosted instance) has published openly — WITHOUT any BROWSERTRIX_USER/PASSWORD/TOKEN. Today `import browsertrix` always logs in (JWT bearer), so public content held by an org you don't have an account on is unreachable, even though Browsertrix exposes it through an unauthenticated API.

## Public API (base https://app.browsertrix.com, verified v1.23.0)
1. `GET /api/public/orgs/{orgSlug}/collections` → `{org, collections[]}`; each collection has `id`, `oid`, `slug`, `name`, `totalSize`, `crawlCount`, `pageCount`, `allowPublicDownload`. (`resources` is empty here.)
2. `GET /api/orgs/{oid}/collections/{collId}/public/replay.json` → `resources[]`, one per WACZ: `path` (presigned S3, range-capable HTTP 206, expires ~48h), `hash` (sha256), `size`, `name`, `crawlId`.
3. `GET /api/public/orgs/{orgSlug}/collections/{collSlug}/download` → stable, token-free WACZ. GET-only, ignores Range (whole-file stream). For a multi-crawl collection this is a MULTI-WACZ (nested .wacz) — nested-WACZ indexing landed in rustyweb-15z.8 (#51), so this path now works.

Two ways in, both viable:
- per-crawl `resources[].path` — flat single WACZs, index cleanly, but presigned URLs expire ~48h (fine once downloaded to <home>/archive).
- collection `/download` — one nested multi-WACZ, token-free/stable, needs the nested-WACZ support we now have.

## Proposed shape
- Public-mode flag, e.g. `import browsertrix --public --org <orgSlug> [--collection <collSlug>]`, that skips login and hits the `/api/public/...` endpoints. No credentials read; error clearly if credentials are supplied alongside --public (they're ignored).
- Reuse the existing download-and-index flow (durable copy under <home>/archive, whole-file fixity) and the metadata seeding from rustyweb-15z.6 (org name → creator, collection description/tags/dates → finding aid). The public collections payload carries name/slug and counts; confirm it also exposes description/caption/tags/date range for seeding (may be a thinner object than the authenticated one — degrade gracefully).
- Respect `allowPublicDownload`: if false, skip/refuse with a clear message.
- Add the two/three public endpoints to the `browsertrix.rs` client behind the existing `Transport` trait; keep auth optional (public transport sends no Authorization header).
- Provenance/incremental (rustyweb-15z.5) should work the same via the Browsertrix item/crawl ids.

## Tests / verification
- Extend the mock Browsertrix server in tests with the `/api/public/...` routes; assert a `--public` import needs no env credentials, seeds the finding aid, and skips already-imported crawls on re-run.
- Manual smoke against a real public org (e.g. `usgov-archive`, Webrecorder's US Gov Web Archive — 15 public collections).

Relates to rustyweb-15z.6 (metadata seeding) and rustyweb-15z.8 (nested multi-WACZ, prerequisite for the collection `/download` path, now landed).

title: Index nested (multi-)WACZ files
description:
WACZ files can nest: a multi-WACZ is a ZIP whose datapackage.json lists other .wacz files (conventionally under data/) as resources, with no top-level archive/ WARCs. This is exactly what Browsertrix's public collection /download endpoint returns for any collection with >1 crawl.

rustyweb's indexer currently assumes a flat single-level WACZ and would SILENTLY index a multi-WACZ as empty (no error):
- wacz.rs iter_warc_paths (~L257) only yields entries under archive/ ending in .warc.gz/.warc; a multi-WACZ has none.
- find_cdx_entry/search_cdx read the single top-level CDX; read_datapackage reads the single top-level datapackage.json.
Replay is unaffected: wabac.js/ReplayWeb.page already resolves nested WACZs via range reads. The gap is indexing-only.

Scope:
- Detect the multi-WACZ case in wacz.rs (datapackage resources are .wacz, or no archive/ WARCs but .wacz entries exist).
- Recurse into each nested .wacz entry (extract to temp) to pull its WARCs, CDX, and pages for full-text + CDX indexing.
- Recommended approach A (recurse and flatten): keep one Wacz manifest entry per outer file; index all nested content. Alternative B (explode nested WACZs into Collection members) deferred; member file-resolution is trickier since members are ZIP entries, not files.
- Add a multi-WACZ fixture + test. Real fixture available: Browsertrix public /download for a multi-crawl collection, e.g. climate-economic-justice-screening-tool (3 crawls).
- Note in code/docs that replay already handles nesting.

Prerequisite for the simpler Browsertrix import path (one combined /download per collection instead of enumerating + downloading each crawl WACZ).

title: Streaming import + refreshable-remote replay for Browsertrix (index-only footprint)
description:
Optional alternative to the always-download flow (15z.3), for self-hosters who want an INDEX-ONLY footprint: stream-index a Browsertrix WACZ from its presigned replay.json URL WITHOUT downloading, and keep replay working despite ~48h presigned-URL expiry.

Supersedes the naive closed 15z.4 (which indexed the presigned URL as a plain Url source): that is not durable because a baked-in signed URL dies in ~48h and replay breaks. The fix is a REFRESHABLE-REMOTE source that re-signs on demand.

Design:
- New Source variant storing the STABLE identity (host + org id + item/crawl id + resource name/hash), not a fixed signed URL.
- Index: resolve a fresh presigned URL, stream-index in place (download=false) — reuses the existing Url/streaming path + http_range range GETs.
- Replay: make viewer_source point at /files/{id} for this source (as for local files); serve_file re-resolves a fresh presigned URL and 302-redirects to it (fits the existing remote-redirect pattern at server.rs ~706). Cache the signed URL until near expiry so we do not re-auth per range request.
- serve needs Browsertrix credentials/config to re-sign (env or a config file under <home>). This is the real operational cost: fine for a self-hoster indexing their own org; a bigger decision for a public/shared instance. Strictly opt-in; download-for-durability (15z.3) stays the default.
- Handle refresh failures gracefully (creds rotated / item deleted / Browsertrix down) with a clear replay-time error.

Contrast with stable remote URLs (e.g. SUCHO on S3): those already stream-index AND remote-replay today via a plain Url source with no refresh needed — this task is only about the EXPIRING-URL case. Depends conceptually on 15z.1 (client resolves resources). Files: collections.rs (Source), index.rs, server.rs (serve_file/viewer_source), main.rs/config, DESIGN.md.
close_reason: Landed in PR #53: Source::Browsertrix + SourceResolver; import --stream (index-only); on-demand re-resolution for replay (24h cache + stale-token self-heal); local/remote source pills. Verified live against real Browsertrix.

title: Delete a crawl or a collection (remove files + update the index)
description:
Add commands to remove content, keeping the archive folder, the manifest, and the Tantivy index consistent:
- `rustyweb crawl delete <id> [--home] [--yes]`
- `rustyweb collection delete <id|name> [--with-crawls] [--home] [--yes]`
(mirrors the existing `crawl set` / `collection set|list`).

CRAWL DELETE must remove, as one consistent operation:
1. The Tantivy documents for that crawl — delete by term on the crawl_id field, then commit. (Verify crawl_id is a term-indexed field usable with delete_term; add a delete path to SearchIndex if missing.)
2. The manifest Wacz entry (collections.rs / Manifest).
3. The local WACZ file under <home>/archive — ONLY for a File source (a Url source has no local file); guard against deleting a file still referenced by another entry.
4. The cached thumbnail (<home>/index/thumbs/<crawl_id>.jpg and .pinned) — overlaps with rustyweb-thumb-gc-2x5c.
Then, if the crawl was the last member of its collection, decide: drop the now-empty collection or keep it.

COLLECTION DELETE — decide/settle the semantics (flag it for the maintainer):
- default: delete the collection GROUPING only, leaving its crawls (reassign each to its own singleton collection, id==crawl id); OR
- `--with-crawls`: also delete every member crawl (files + index docs) as above.

TRICKY PARTS (why this needs care):
- Tantivy deletes are term-based and only take effect on commit; disk space is reclaimed only on segment merge, so the index wont shrink immediately (document this; a follow-up could force a merge).
- Consistency/atomicity: a crash mid-delete can orphan a file or leave stale index docs. Pick an order (delete index docs+commit → save manifest → delete file/thumb last) and tolerate a re-run cleaning up leftovers. Relates to rustyweb-atomic-reindex-7x3j.
- Destructive: require confirmation unless --yes; print exactly what will be removed (file paths, doc counts).
- Idempotence: deleting an unknown id is a clear error; a partially-deleted crawl can be re-deleted to finish cleanup.

Files: search.rs (delete-by-term + commit), collections.rs (Manifest removal helpers), index.rs (orchestration: delete_crawl/delete_collection), main.rs (CLI + confirmation), thumbnail.rs (remove thumb), DESIGN.md/README. Tests: index a fixture, delete it, assert it is gone from search + manifest + disk, and that a reindex does not resurrect it.

title: Admin / management mode: create collections & add crawls from the browser
description:
Give indice a write surface so a non-CLI user can create/edit collections and add crawls from a browser, WITHOUT the Tauri desktop shell.

WHY NOW (decision, edsu 2026-08-03): the desktop-app epic (rustyweb-desktop-app-i91t) is a packaging concern — it wraps an experience that today has no front door for creating collections or adding crawls. Those admin workflows are the actual unlock and are what a desktop app would eventually sit on top of. So we PAUSE the Tauri track and build the admin backend + a browser admin UI first.

KEY ARCHITECTURAL FINDING (backend survey 2026-08-03): the write surface is INDEPENDENT of Tauri. Today all mutation is CLI-only; the HTTP server is deliberately read-only (opens Tantivy read-only at server.rs:63 so the CLI can hold the write lock). But the library-level write primitives already exist and are clean (home, ...) fns: index::index_location (add crawl, auto-creates collection), index::set_collection (create/edit finding aid), seed_collection, set_crawl_note, thumbnails. The gap is purely the HTTP/transport + writer-locking + auth layer. The existing 'management mode' design (serve --manage, opt-in, default read-only) was already meant to be shared by CLI and app — so it runs fine in a plain browser. Tauri only adds a native file-picker (index-in-place by path vs byte-upload) + double-click packaging.

SCOPE
- Management-mode server endpoints (add crawl) — rustyweb-desktop-app-i91t.3 (re-homed here, decoupled from the app shell).
- Collection write endpoints (create/edit finding aid) — NEW, was unticketed.
- Browser admin UI (forms/pages served under --manage) — NEW; generalizes the desktop-flavored empty-state (i91t.4).
- Delete over HTTP — layered on rustyweb-71im (CLI delete primitive) once that lands.

AUTH DECISION (open): default serve --manage is fine unauthenticated for localhost/single-user. The moment the management surface is reachable off-localhost it needs auth. Decide the model before exposing writes on a bound address (see the auth-decision task).

title: Decide auth model for the management write surface

title: Atomic reindex: build into temp dir and swap, so a failed rebuild never touches the working index
description:
reindex currently rebuilds the full-text index destructively and in place: it deletes index/full_text up front, then recreates it from the manifest sources. If the rebuild fails partway (a remote source down, a crash, disk full, process killed), you are left with a partial index — worse than before you started. The resilient-reindex work (rustyweb-reindex-resilient-aev) softened this: a source that fails after retries is now skipped with a warning and reindex still commits a usable-but-incomplete index and exits non-zero. But the working index is still mutated in place, so a hard failure (crash/kill mid-rebuild, not a per-source error) can still leave it degraded.

Make reindex atomic: build the new index into a sibling temp dir (e.g. index/full_text.new) and swap it in with an atomic rename only once the rebuild fully succeeds. On any failure, the existing index/full_text is left untouched — you are never worse off than before the reindex.

Notes / considerations:
- No copy of the old index is needed. reindex already builds the new full-text index from scratch from the sources, so "build into temp" just means writing that fresh build to a sibling path instead of overwriting in place. Cost is transient extra disk: old + new full_text coexist until the swap (~2x full-text index size for the duration).
- Swap: build into <index>/full_text.new, then rename old -> full_text.old (or remove), rename new -> full_text. rename on the same filesystem is atomic. Clean up any stale .new/.old dirs from a previous interrupted run at start.
- Interaction with skip-on-failure: decide the policy when some sources were skipped. Options: still swap in the partial index (current behavior: usable but incomplete) but from the temp dir, OR only swap when 0 sources were skipped and otherwise keep the old index + exit non-zero. Leaning toward: swap in the partial rebuild (so a mostly-good rebuild still lands) but keep exiting non-zero — preserves today's semantics while removing the mid-rebuild-crash risk. Confirm with maintainer.
- Manifest (collections.json / waczs.json) is separate and tiny; keep its save ordered so it stays consistent with whichever index is live after the swap.
- Tests: simulate a failure after the temp index is partly built and assert the original index is still intact and searchable; assert a successful reindex swaps cleanly and leaves no .new/.old dirs.

Follow-up to rustyweb-reindex-resilient-aev (now closed). Ties to the shareable/self-serve goal (a reindex on someone else's box shouldn't be able to destroy their working index).

title: Web archive authenticity (WACZ signatures)
description: Future work on verifiable authenticity, distinct from provenance. A signed WACZ carries a datapackage-digest.json with a hash + cryptographic signature of datapackage.json (webrecorder WACZ auth spec). Two stages: (a) detect and display presence of a signature (no crypto deps); (b) verify the signature against the datapackage (public-key or certificate-signed; needs crypto). Complements the existing sha256 fixity (verify command). Moved out of the provenance epic (was rustyweb-provenance-imd.4) so provenance can wrap up.

title: Detect and display WACZ signature
description: Detect datapackage-digest.json in the WACZ and show a signed/verified status on the collection page alongside the sha256 fixity. Stage (a): detect + display presence (no crypto). Full cryptographic verification is a follow-on stage (b).

title: Verify downloaded WACZ against the Browsertrix replay.json hash
description:
Split out of the (now closed) Browsertrix importer epic rustyweb-15z as standalone follow-up.

The Browsertrix importer downloads each WACZ from its presigned replay.json URL but does not verify the bytes against the resource hash the API provides (replay.json resources[].hash, e.g. sha256:...). The .part->rename dance guards against a partial/truncated write, and indexing records its own SHA-256 (so `rustyweb verify` can detect later corruption) -- but we do not catch a silently-wrong/corrupt download AT import time, against the source-of-truth hash.

Confirmed on main (2026-07): res.hash is parsed from replay.json and stored for provenance / incremental-sync keys (set_browsertrix_provenance_by_id, seen keys), but the downloaded bytes are never compared to it. run_verify only re-hashes against the manifest's own computed sha256, not against Browsertrix's advertised hash.

Add: after download_wacz, compute the SHA-256 of the downloaded file and compare to res.hash (strip the 'sha256:' prefix); on mismatch, delete the file and error out for that item (do not index). Reuse collections::file_sha256. Cheap (one pass over the just-written file) and turns a bad download into an immediate, clear failure instead of a subtly broken crawl.

Files: main.rs (download_wacz / run_browsertrix). Small; add a unit or e2e assertion (serve wrong bytes -> import errors).

title: Facet on hostname in addition to site (registrable domain)

Add a facet on the full HOSTNAME too, so meaningful subdomains are distinguishable: library.stanford.edu, exhibits.stanford.edu, sul.stanford.edu all collapse to "stanford.edu" today, which hides useful structure for large multi-subdomain institutions.

- Surface it: add host to the facet overview (facet_overview_scoped) and the facet UI (views.rs/server.rs), alongside site.
- Design choice to settle: two independent facets (site AND host), or a single HIERARCHICAL facet path (site → host, e.g. /stanford.edu/exhibits.stanford.edu) that gives both levels in one collapsible tree. Hierarchy reads better for the stanford.edu case; note host cardinality can be high, so consider top-N + counts.
- Keep site faceting as-is; host is additive.

Files: search.rs (schema field + extraction + facet aggregation), views.rs + server.rs (facet UI + query filter, e.g. host: alias like the existing crawl: alias), DESIGN.md/README (note the new facet + that it needs a reindex). Relates to the crawl/site faceting already present.

title: Group collection members by site on the collection detail page
description:
On the collection detail page, group member crawls by site instead of showing every crawl as its own tile.

Context: the collection detail page now shows a grid of member crawls, each with its representative image (rustyweb-crawl-thumbnail-s1ff). A collection often contains repeat crawls of the SAME site over time, which share the same og:image, so the grid can look repetitive (e.g. 10 near-identical tiles for one site crawled 10 times).

Idea: collapse members by site (registrable domain, the same `site` value the Site facet uses) into one tile per site, with:
- a representative image (any member's thumbnail for that site),
- a "crawled N times" badge / capture date range,
- expand to the individual crawls (or link to a site-scoped view / search).

Considerations:
- Grouping key: registrable domain (site) vs exact host (domain) vs seed URL. Site (eTLD+1) is probably right, matching the Site facet.
- A collection can legitimately mix many one-off sites (no repeats) — in that case grouping is a no-op and the flat grid is fine, so only group where it reduces clutter.
- Ordering: by most-recent capture, or by crawl count.
- Interaction: clicking a site tile could go to a search scoped to collection + site (collection:<slug> site:<host>), which already works, or to an expanded member list.
- Ties into the two-level collection model and could inform a future "site" as a first-class grouping level.

title: Per-page og:image gallery on the crawl detail page
description:
Collect the per-page og:image for every page in a crawl (not just the main page) and show a small gallery of those distinct images on the crawl detail page.

Motivation: a crawl covers many pages, each of which may declare its own OpenGraph image (`<meta property="og:image">`). Those are curated, page-level representative images — unlike arbitrary captured resources (icons/pixels/sprites), so no size/noise filtering is needed. A gallery of them gives a rich, honest visual overview of what a crawl contains, and photographs well.

Builds directly on rustyweb-crawl-thumbnail-s1ff, which already:
- extracts og:image per HTML record (search::extract_html_text -> HtmlText.og_image) — currently only the MAIN page's is used;
- has the fetch -> decode -> downscale -> cache pipeline (thumbnail.rs) and the /thumb serving route + CSS.

Scope for a future v1 (keep bounded):
- During indexing, collect og:image across pages, resolve each against its page URL, and DEDUP by resolved image URL (many pages share one site-wide default og:image, so distinct images are what matter).
- Cap the set per crawl (e.g. <= 12-24 distinct images) to bound index time + disk.
- Cache each as a downscaled thumbnail (e.g. <home>/index/thumbs/<crawl_id>/<n>.jpg) and record the set on the manifest, or a manifest sidecar.
- Serve them (extend the /thumb route to an indexed set, or a per-crawl gallery listing) and render a strip/grid on the crawl detail page. The single representative image (main page og:image) stays as the card/hero.
- Graceful: crawls with no per-page og:images just show the single representative image (or placeholder).

Considerations:
- Dedup + cap ordering: prefer distinct images; order by page order / seed pages first.
- Storage growth: N thumbnails per crawl * many crawls — keep N small; needs a reindex to populate.
- This is the "keep it simple, page-level OpenGraph metadata" version the maintainer wanted — explicitly NOT a dump of all captured image resources (that raw-gallery idea was considered and rejected as noisy/expensive).

Relates to s1ff (done) and rustyweb-collection-group-by-site-mwg1. Priority: future / P3.

title: Representative image/thumbnail for collection cards, collection detail, and crawl detail (from WACZ screenshots)
description:
Idea (maintainer): use a representative image to make collection cards and detail pages (and crawl detail pages) more visual -- rather than the current text-only cards/lists. This matters for the shareable/adoption story and for the blog post's screenshots.

Source of the image: Browsertrix WACZs often contain page screenshots, stored as WARC resource records (target URIs like `urn:view:<url>`, `urn:thumbnail:<url>`, `urn:screenshot:<url>`, image/png|jpeg payloads). We already consume a sibling record type -- Browsertrix's rendered-text `urn:text:` records (index.rs:674+, RenderedText) -- so this extends that same pattern to image records. Verify the exact URN scheme / content types against a real Browsertrix WACZ before committing to field names.

Scope (v1, keep it small):
- Pick ONE representative image per crawl (WACZ): e.g. the thumbnail/screenshot of the seed page (first page in pages.jsonl), preferring `urn:thumbnail:` if present (small) else downsizing a larger screenshot. Don't ingest all screenshots.
- Store just enough to serve it: record the chosen image's location (which inner WARC + offset/length, consistent with CDX-guided extraction) on the crawl's manifest entry, OR extract+cache the bytes under <home>/index (decide; caching avoids a range fetch on every card render but costs disk). Lean toward a small cached thumbnail (e.g. index/thumbs/{wacz_id}.jpg) so serving is cheap and works for local + remote sources uniformly.
- Serve it: a route like /thumb/{wacz_id} (or /crawl/{id}/thumb) returning the cached image with caching headers, mirroring serve_embedded_asset's ETag/Cache-Control.
- Display it: collection card (homepage), collection detail (a representative image, likely from one member crawl), and crawl detail. Collection-level image = pick one member's thumbnail (e.g. first/most-recent member) for v1.
- Graceful fallback: many WACZs (esp. non-Browsertrix, e.g. py-wacz) have NO screenshots -- must degrade cleanly to today's text-only card/detail. No broken image boxes.

Considerations:
- Only extract during indexing (index_one), alongside the existing record pass, to avoid a second scan. Optional flag to disable (privacy/size).
- Size/perf: thumbnails should be small (cap dimensions/bytes); consider re-encoding to JPEG/WebP. Adds an image dep (e.g. `image` crate) -- weigh against the single-binary/pure-Rust ethos (image is pure Rust; OK).
- Privacy/appropriateness: a screenshot may show sensitive content; keep it opt-outable and only use the seed/representative page.

Relates to the vocab rename (crawls-captures-vocab-b1e) and faceted detail pages (facets-detail-pages-dgr) -- together these are the collection/crawl view polish pass. Ties to the Browsertrix importer epic (15z), which brings in exactly these screenshot-bearing WACZs.

Pipeline: at index time (CDX-streamable WACZs), thumbnail::generate reads the main page's HTML, extracts og:image, range-fetches that captured image from the WACZ, downscales it (image crate, 400px), and caches <home>/index/thumbs/<crawl_id>.jpg. Served at GET /thumb/{id}; shown on collection cards + collection/crawl detail. No image => CSS-only placeholder (hash-tinted gradient, per the maintainer's suggestion). Best-effort throughout; needs a reindex to populate. Screenshot-source + per-collection curated images remain follow-ups.

title: Vocabulary: Crawls / Captures vs WACZ in the UI
description:
Question (maintainer): do users care more about "Crawls" or "Captures" than about a "WACZ"?

WACZ is a packaging format -- a technical container. Users of a web archive more likely think in terms of:
- Crawls: a crawl session (e.g. a Browsertrix crawl) -- the user-meaningful activity that produced the content. Often 1:1 with a WACZ today, but not necessarily (a WACZ could bundle multiple crawls; a crawl could span WACZs).
- Captures / mementos: individual snapshots of a URL at a point in time -- what users navigate temporally (repeat captures of the same URL over time; already grouped in results, per the Costa & Silva navigational/temporal finding cited in DESIGN).

This is an information-architecture / vocabulary decision, not (yet) code: audit where the UI foregrounds "WACZ" and decide whether "Crawl" and/or "Capture" would be clearer -- e.g. presenting a WACZ as a "crawl" in provenance/collection contexts while keeping "WACZ" only where the file/format is actually meant (downloads, fixity, replay source). Ties to the two-level collection model and the provenance framing (Maemura et al.).

Worth deciding the mental model rustyweb presents before layering more UI (facets on detail pages, cross-WACZ discovery) on top of it, since those features inherit whatever vocabulary we choose. Discussion/decision issue; the outcome may spawn concrete rename/relabel tasks.

title: Cross-WACZ link resolution during replay
description:
Problem: replay is WACZ-direct and scoped to ONE WACZ. The viewer loads a single source (viewer_source(col) -> /replay/viewer?source=<wacz>&url=&ts=), so wabac.js resolves links only within that WACZ. If a replayed page links to a URL that isn't in the loaded WACZ but IS archived in ANOTHER WACZ in the collection/archive, the link fails to replay -- even though rustyweb has that URL indexed elsewhere. This undercuts the "reading room" goal of navigating the archive as a whole.

What we already have to build on:
- Tantivy index maps url -> collection/WACZ (+ timestamp) for indexed PAGES (fast, exact-match lookup on the url field).
- search-url opens each WACZ's internal CDX and returns records matching a URL, so it can resolve ANY archived URL (not just pages) to the WACZ(s) that hold it -- at the cost of reading CDXs.

Candidate approaches (to evaluate):
1. Index-driven redirect (lightweight): add a resolve API (e.g. GET /api/resolve?url= -> [{wacz_id, ts}]) backed by the index for pages. When a replayed page navigates to a URL the current WACZ lacks, consult the API and re-launch the viewer against the WACZ that has it (a "this link lives in another crawl -- open it" jump). Low browser footprint; needs a way to detect the miss / intercept navigation inside ReplayWeb.page.
2. Multi-WACZ collection replay (native): load a ReplayWeb.page multi-WACZ collection (a JSON manifest listing the collection's member WACZ sources) instead of a single WACZ, so wabac.js merges their indexes and resolves any URL present in the collection natively. Cleanest UX; but the browser loads each member WACZ's index -- a scale concern for large/institutional collections. VERIFY ReplayWeb.page multi-WACZ support + how it scopes/loads indexes.
3. Hybrid / lazy: start with the page's own WACZ; on a miss, resolve via the index and dynamically add the target WACZ to the wabac collection, so only WACZs actually needed get loaded.

Open questions:
- How to detect a cross-WACZ miss / hook link navigation inside the ReplayWeb.page iframe (does it expose events / postMessage, or do we intercept clicks pre-replay?).
- Page-level resolution (the click-a-link case) vs full resource-level (sub-resources like images/CSS from another WACZ) -- the latter is deeper and likely out of scope for v1.
- Scale: avoid loading an entire large collection's indexes into the browser (ties to rustyweb-scale-footprint-qw5).
- Which URL/timestamp to pick when multiple WACZs/captures have the target (closest in time? most recent? same collection first?).

Scope note: v1 could target page-to-page links within a single curated collection, resolved via the index, as the highest-value slice. Relates to the two-level collection model, search-url, and the outbound-links link-graph task (rustyweb-outbound-links-ind).
close_reason: WON'T FIX (maintainer decision, 2026-07-26): resolution WITHIN a collection is acceptable, so the explicit 'archived in another crawl - open it?' affordance won't be built. Multi-WACZ collection replay (bukh Phase 1 + qw5.10) already resolves links across a collection's member WACZs via wabac's pagesQueryUrl (/collection/{id}/pages) - silently, scoped to the collection; that within-collection resolution is the accepted model. Sub-resource transclusion stays out (role-2 lookup is destination-gated to page navigations), preserving per-page temporal coherence. The blocks-dependency on federation-shwl.3 (/api/resolve) is moot for dk4; that endpoint remains its own federation task.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Design caution (temporal coherence): relevant prior work from Michael Nelson's team at ODU (the WS-DL group) on temporal violations in composite mementos -- a replayed page can stitch together embedded resources captured at different times, yielding a composite that never actually existed as presented. See Ainsworth, Nelson & Van de Sompel, "Only One Out of Five Archived Web Pages Existed as Presented" (ACM Hypertext 2015), and the broader WS-DL work on temporal coherence / prima facie violations (the Internet Archive Wayback Machine transcluding older captures of embedded resources into a page).

Why it matters here: cross-WACZ resolution deliberately pulls a URL from a DIFFERENT WACZ -- i.e. a different crawl at a (possibly very) different time. Doing so can INTRODUCE exactly these temporal violations, presenting a page that never existed. So the "which WACZ/timestamp to pick" open question above is not just a convenience choice -- it is a correctness concern:
- Prefer captures close to the root page's memento-datetime; bound and/or surface the temporal spread to the user rather than silently substituting a far-off capture.
- Page-to-page link navigation (following a link to another archived page) is lower risk than transcluding a sub-resource (image/CSS/JS) from another WACZ into the current page -- the latter is the classic temporal-violation case and should be treated with extra caution (or left out of v1).
- Consider making cross-WACZ substitution visible/optional (e.g. "this link is archived in another crawl from <date> -- open it?") rather than seamless, so the user knows they've crossed a temporal boundary.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Design reframing (maintainer): single-WACZ replay scope is a FEATURE, not a bug. Because replay is scoped to one WACZ, a rendered page only pulls resources captured in that same crawl -- which is precisely what preserves temporal coherence and avoids the ODU-documented temporal violations (a page stitched from resources of different times that never existed as presented). Pulling a JS file or image from another time period into the page would be the bug; NOT doing so is the virtue.

Consequences for this feature:
- Do NOT merge WACZs for replay or transclude sub-resources (JS/CSS/images) across WACZs -- that would recreate the temporal-violation problem. This deprioritizes the "native multi-WACZ merged replay" approach and rules out cross-WACZ sub-resource resolution.
- Reframe the cross-WACZ case around MISSING PAGES (link targets), not resources: when a link's target isn't in the current WACZ, use the index to surface where else in the archive it was captured -- list the other WACZs/crawls that hold it, WITH their capture dates and provenance -- as an explicit discovery affordance. Opening one starts a fresh, temporally-coherent single-WACZ replay in THAT crawl's context.
- Make the temporal/provenance boundary explicit: the goal is to let the user consciously choose to look at another capture, understanding the crawl context is changing -- not to silently substitute content into the current page.

Net: this is primarily a DISCOVERY feature (fits the reading-room ethos: "this link isn't in this crawl; here's where else in the archive to find it, and when it was captured"), layered on index lookups -- not a replay-fidelity change. Single-WACZ replay stays coherent and untouched.

Documentation: when this is implemented, note the connection to web-archives research in README.md and DESIGN.md -- both temporal coherence / temporal violations (ODU WS-DL; Ainsworth, Nelson & Van de Sompel, HT 2015) and the framing of single-WACZ scope as a coherence feature. DESIGN.md already grounds the discovery features in the literature (Costa & Silva; Maemura et al.; the SHINE / SolrWayback lineage), so this fits alongside them.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Plan (wabac `pagesQueryUrl` mechanism + how it reconciles with the single-WACZ / temporal-coherence stance above)

## New intel: wabac.js has a server-side page-list API (`pagesQueryUrl`)
Reverse-engineered from the vendored bundle (replaywebpage 2.4.6, crates/rustyweb-lib/static/replay/sw.js). A collection can carry `metadata.pagesQueryUrl` (also read from a multi-WACZ replay.json). When set, wabac STOPS loading pages from the WACZ (`if(!this.pagesQueryUrl){…load pages.jsonl…}`) and calls the server instead. It is used in TWO distinct roles:

1. Page list + search (`queryPages`): `GET <pagesQueryUrl>?search=<q>&page=<n>&pageSize=<25>` → `200 {"total":N,"items":[{"url","ts"|"date","title","filename"},…]}`. Powers the viewer's Pages sidebar and in-replay search. Purely informational — no resources are transcluded.

2. URL→WACZ resolution for on-demand replay (`getWACZFilesForPagesQuery`): `GET <pagesQueryUrl>?url=<exact>&pageSize=25` (falls back to `?search=<url>`) → `items[].filename` → the member WACZ(s) holding that URL; wabac then lazily loads ONLY those WACZ files and serves the resource from them. `item.filename` must match a WACZ `name` in the collection's replay.json resource list.

This is the Browsertrix pattern — their public replay.json carries `pagesQueryUrl` pointing at their `/pages` API (we saw it on usgov-archive).

## The catch (re: the temporal-coherence reframing above)
Role 2 is exactly the cross-WACZ sub-resource transclusion this ticket rules out: wabac resolves ANY requested URL (incl. images/CSS/JS) to whichever WACZ has it and loads it into the current page — recreating the ODU temporal-violation problem. So we must NOT flip replay to a native merged multiwacz-with-pagesQueryUrl collection. That would undo the single-WACZ virtue.

## Proposed design: adopt role 1, not role 2
Keep rendering single-WACZ (temporally coherent). Use rustyweb's index only for discovery, via one endpoint that happens to be wabac-`pagesQueryUrl`-shaped so it can also feed the viewer's page list/search:

- New endpoint `GET /replay/<coll>/pages?search=&url=&page=&pageSize=` answered from the Tantivy index (we already map url→crawl/WACZ+ts, and have title/ts/collection). Returns `{total, items:[{url, ts, title, filename}]}`, `filename` = the crawl's WACZ resource name.
- Wire it as the collection's `pagesQueryUrl` ONLY to power the collection-wide **page list + search sidebar** in the existing single-WACZ viewer (role 1). This is a straight win: search/browse the whole collection's pages from the index, without loading pages.jsonl.
- For the **missing-link case** (the reframed core of this ticket): when a link target isn't in the current WACZ, hit the SAME endpoint (`?url=`) to find which other crawl(s) hold it, and surface an explicit "archived in another crawl from <date> — open it?" affordance (with provenance). Opening one launches a fresh single-WACZ replay in THAT crawl (approach #1 in the description). No transclusion; the temporal boundary is visible and user-chosen.
- Prefer captures closest to the current memento-datetime; show the temporal spread (per the temporal-coherence comment).

Open verification items:
- Confirm whether setting `pagesQueryUrl` on the viewer's single-WACZ collection triggers wabac's role-2 resource resolution at all, or only the page-list/search. If it can't be cleanly separated, drive the page list + miss-detection ourselves (UI/postMessage) and keep the endpoint purely as our own resolve API (overlaps rustyweb-federation-shwl.3 `/api/resolve`).
- How to detect the link miss / hook navigation inside the ReplayWeb.page iframe (still the key UX unknown from the description).
- Pin behavior to the vendored wabac version + add a replay test.

## Relationship to rustyweb-scale-footprint-qw5
Bidirectional, and the reason to prefer the server-side pages endpoint over loading pages.jsonl client-side:
- This IS the replay-client instance of qw5's "laptop→institutional TBs" goal. A large collection (e.g. usgov-archive's 570k-page collections) can't load its full page list into the browser's IndexedDB; `pagesQueryUrl` paginates server-side so the replay-client footprint stays flat regardless of collection size — complementing qw5's focus on the server index footprint.
- The pages endpoint is a paginated, searchable query over the SAME Tantivy index qw5 is modeling, so its cost belongs in qw5.5 (query-time cost of faceting/grouping at scale) as a new consumer, and qw5.3 (cap stored body text) bounds how cheaply it can return titles/snippets.
- Its latency depends on the index being compacted — a fragmented index makes this query slow the same way it slowed search (see qw5.9 optimize/merge). So dk4-via-pagesQueryUrl is ENABLED BY qw5's index being scale-ready and is itself a qw5-aligned scale win on the client side.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Clarification (request flow — does replay phone home per URL?): No. Normal resource replay stays WACZ-direct and does NOT round-trip to the rustyweb API per URL:
- Rendering the current page: wabac loads that ONE WACZ's index into the browser and resolves the page's own resources (HTML/img/CSS/JS) locally, fetching bytes via range reads on /files/{id} (a dumb byte server, not a resolve API). Unchanged from today.
- The pages API (pagesQueryUrl-shaped endpoint) is hit only on occasional, user-driven events: (a) the page-list/search sidebar (paginated, per user action), and (b) a cross-WACZ link MISS (only when a link target isn't in the current WACZ). Never per sub-resource.

Explicitly NOT adopted (these WOULD talk back per URL): wabac's `remotewarcproxy` source (fetches H/<url>+A/<url> from the server for every resource), and native multiwacz + pagesQueryUrl "role 2" (resolves each requested URL, incl. sub-resources, to a WACZ via the API and lazy-loads it) — the latter also being the temporal-violation trap.

Caveat to verify: setting pagesQueryUrl on the collection to get the sidebar MIGHT also switch on wabac's per-URL role-2 resolution — couldn't confirm from the minified bundle whether they separate. If not, fallback is to NOT set pagesQueryUrl and instead drive the sidebar + miss-detection ourselves (viewer/postMessage), so the API is touched only on explicit user actions. Either way the guarantee holds: normal resource replay does not round-trip to the API per URL.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Aligns with rustyweb-homepage-replay-bukh (2026-07-25): both need the SAME missing primitive — a collection-level (multi-WACZ) replay. bukh's core builds it (homepage 'replay a collection'); dk4 layers cross-WACZ discovery on top. bukh naturally precedes dk4. Linked as related.

== Consolidated sw.js trace (replaywebpage 2.4.6, class Gb = multi-WACZ loader). Supersedes the earlier 'couldn't confirm from the minified bundle whether roles separate' open item. ==

MULTI-WACZ COLLECTION FORMAT (loadWACZFiles): a JSON doc with resources:[{name,path,hash,crawlId}] (+ optional metadata.pagesQueryUrl / preloadResources / textIndex / total). Same family as Browsertrix replay.json. Each path = a WACZ location -> maps directly onto rustyweb /files/{id} (local) or presigned/remote URL (streamed); members can independently be local or remote.

ROLE 2 (per-URL server resolution) IS DESTINATION-GATED — the sub-resource temporal-violation fear was OVERSTATED. getWACZFilesToTry sets the URL-to-resolve (r=t.url) only when destination is 'document'/'iframe' (top-level page nav); sub-resources (image/style/script/font) never reach getWACZFilesForPagesQuery. So cross-WACZ sub-resource transclusion (the ODU temporal-violation trap) does NOT happen via pagesQueryUrl. Only page navigations resolve across WACZs.

BUT two things still couple the roles:
1. Role 2 is SILENT, not explicit: a page-nav to a URL not in the current WACZ auto-resolves (?url=<href>&pageSize=25, falls back to ?search=) and lazy-loads that WACZ — no 'open it? from <date>' prompt. That's the explicit temporal-boundary UX dk4 wants; you can't get the Pages sidebar (role 1) via pagesQueryUrl without also getting this silent page-jump.
2. The machinery is json/multiwacz-gated ('json'===rootSourceType; retryLoad early-returns otherwise). Using pagesQueryUrl at all requires switching the viewer from single-WACZ to a multi-WACZ json collection.

TWO-MODE SCALE TABLE (shared with bukh, ties to qw5):
- multi-WACZ, NO pagesQueryUrl: wabac loads every member WACZ index client-side; native cross-WACZ page+subresource resolution; OK small, infeasible large.
- multi-WACZ + pagesQueryUrl: wabac skips per-WACZ page lists, defers URL->WACZ to the server endpoint, lazily loads only needed members; flat browser footprint; the only viable large-collection path.

CONTRACT if we set pagesQueryUrl (wabac appends): ?url=<exact>, ?search=<q> (fallback + page-list search), ?page=<n>, ?pageSize=25; expects {total, items:[{url, ts|date, title, filename}]} where item.filename must match a member WACZ name. Path is NOT prescribed (comes from metadata.pagesQueryUrl) — could be /replay/{coll}/pages or a global /api/resolve (sibling to the existing /api/search).

DESIGN CHOICE: (A) go multi-WACZ + pagesQueryUrl = native sidebar + silent cross-WACZ page jumps, sub-resources safe, but off single-WACZ and no explicit affordance; (B) stay single-WACZ, don't set pagesQueryUrl, drive sidebar + miss-detection ourselves (postMessage) against our own /api/resolve = full control over the explicit 'open it?' temporal-boundary UX, more code. Sub-resource safety holds either way, so the real trade is native-but-silent vs custom-but-explicit — a UX/ethos call, not a temporal-safety one.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text: Shared foundation now IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-25, via bukh Phase 1, working tree): collection-level multi-WACZ replay (GET /collection/{id}/replay.json + viewer multiwacz support). dk4's cross-WACZ discovery now layers on this — mostly additive. Reaffirming the stance revision from the sw.js trace: multi-WACZ replay is safe for sub-resources (role-2 lookup is destination-gated to document/iframe), so the earlier 'rules out native multi-WACZ' framing should be softened in the description to 'avoid pagesQueryUrl role-2 SILENT page-jumps if we want the explicit affordance'.

title: Ship as a double-click desktop app for individual (non-CLI) users
description:
Make the tool installable and usable by non-technical individuals with no command line.

CONTEXT
- Today: install = cargo install --git (needs Rust 1.97 toolchain); run = CLI index then serve then open browser manually. Hard wall for non-technical users.
- The UI is already a web app (server-rendered maud in views.rs + client-side ReplayWeb.page). Replay REQUIRES a real browser engine: service worker + IndexedDB + HTTP range over http://. No native GUI today.
- serve opens the index READ-ONLY on purpose (server.rs:63) so it never blocks a concurrent CLI index. So add-archive-from-UI is an OPT-IN management mode, not the default.
- Decision (edsu): target macOS + Windows; full desktop WINDOW via embedded webview (Tauri); add archives in the UI; KEEP CLI index/serve unchanged for institutional/service deployments.

ARCHITECTURE
- New crate crates/indice-app (Tauri v2) depends on indice-lib. Binds axum to 127.0.0.1:0, runs it in-process, opens a window at http://127.0.0.1:<port> (real http origin, NOT tauri:// — so service workers work).
- Management mode is opt-in (serve --manage, default off). CLI stays read-only + unchanged.

TWO FLAGGED RISKS/COSTS
1. macOS WKWebView service-worker support is historically finicky (Windows WebView2 is Chromium, fine). VALIDATED GO by the Phase 0 spike (.1, 2026-07-30): replay works in embedded WKWebView given (a) an Info.plist NSAllowsLocalNetworking ATS exception for http://127.0.0.1 and (b) a real .app bundle identity for a persistent SW data store. No system-browser fallback needed on macOS. Windows/WebView2 still to confirm before packaging.
2. Code signing is the tax on double-click: Apple Developer ID (~$99/yr, notarization) + Windows Authenticode, or Gatekeeper/SmartScreen block it.

RENAME (DONE)
- The rustyweb->indice rename is complete; the product name is LOCKED to "indice". Packaging/branding (.6) is no longer gated on it: the macOS bundle id, signing identity, .dmg/.msi names, release URLs, and app data dir all use "indice".

title: Build a WACZ from WARC files (with metadata) and index it
description:
Let a user point rustyweb at one or more WARC files (.warc/.warc.gz); rustyweb PACKAGES them into a WACZ (with metadata) under <home>/archive and then indexes it through the normal pipeline. This is the "I have WARCs, not WACZs" on-ramp, and the reusable building block for the Archive-It importer (which downloads WARCs, not WACZs).

Flow:
- Input: WARC file paths (or a dir/glob). CLI (e.g. `rustyweb wacz build <warcs> [--title ... --description ... --creator ...]`) or fold into `index` when given .warc inputs.
- Metadata: take from flags; for anything missing, PROMPT interactively (title, description, creator/curator, subjects, rights, dates — align with the finding-aid model, rustyweb-findingaid-aoc3). Non-interactive/CI: require flags or use sensible defaults.
- Build: generate the WACZ zip = datapackage.json (name/title/description/created + our finding-aid fields where present), a CDX index, and pages.jsonl (seed/discovered pages) as available. Reuse warc.rs (record iteration) + existing CDX handling to compute offsets.
- IMPORTANT constraint: store the WARCs in the zip UNCOMPRESSED (STORED, not deflated) so CDX offsets map to byte positions — rustyweb’s CDX-guided streaming/replay depends on this (a deflated WACZ is already rejected; see index tests). 
- Then index the built WACZ as a durable local File source.

Non-trivial: this is WACZ *creation* (rustyweb currently only reads WACZ). Consider whether to shell out to py-wacz vs. implement natively in Rust (prefer native, no runtime dep, reuse warc.rs/wacz.rs). 

Sequencing: start AFTER the Browsertrix importer (rustyweb-15z) lands. Files: new builder module (wacz write), warc.rs, index.rs, main.rs (CLI + prompts), DESIGN.md.

title: Read-only API, Memento interop & federation across rustyweb instances
description:
Give rustyweb a simple read-only HTTP API, Memento (RFC 7089) interop, and federation so different rustyweb instances (and other archives) can discover each other's content. Read-only to start.

KEYSTONE -- persistent replay URLs. Today a replayable page is a query-string URL (/replay/viewer?source=/files/{id}&url=&ts=&name=&collection=&collection_id=): instance-local, not persistent, and it redundantly encodes name/collection the server could look up. The minimal identity of a memento is (crawl_id, ts, url), and crawl_id is a stable hash of the source. So the persistent URL becomes:
  /crawl/{crawl_id}/{ts}/{url}   e.g. /crawl/a926c132/20220305013545/https://uinp.gov.ua/
It nests under the existing /crawl/{id} detail page (detail vs replay), is bookmarkable/persistent, aligns with single-crawl replay coherence (no composite mementos), and IS a Memento URI-M. Name/collection breadcrumb are looked up server-side from the manifest. This same URL is what the API returns, Memento advertises, and federated peers link to -- so it is built first.

DISCOVERY SUBSTRATE -- web-archive.txt (Mahoney, Terras, Zeller & Lee, "web-archive.txt: A Well-Known Locations Descriptor for Discovery and Coordination of Web Archives", 2026, v0.1). Rather than invent a rustyweb-specific discovery format, adopt web-archive.txt: a TOML descriptor served at /.well-known/web-archive.txt (RFC 8615 well-known URI, content-type text/plain) AND advertised via a Link rel="service-desc" header on the home page. It declares, in four sections: version (version + last_updated); archive identity (id [2-6 lowercase alnum], name inline table w/ en+alt, established, website, email) + archive.organisation (name/type/location ISO-3166/website) + archive.scope (crawl modalities, legal authority + documentation, RFC-3339 temporal coverage interval, domains, and a collections list as id+name inline tables); api (documentation, rate_limit) + api.memento (timemap/timegate endpoint templates + access) + api.cdx (query template + access); and replay state templates (rewritten/no_toolbar/raw). Endpoint templates use {url} + {datetime} (YYYYMMDDhhmmss) placeholders and MAY use {collection} bound to scope.collections.id.

web-archive.txt becomes rustyweb's standard, decentralised identity + capability document: the thing peers read to discover one another (task .5) and the thing external aggregators/validators read. rustyweb PUBLISHES one (new task .9 -- maps its Manifest + collections + Memento routes + persistent replay URL onto the spec's tables) and CONSUMES peers' descriptors for federation config. Because it is a community spec (not rustyweb-specific), rustyweb can federate at the Memento level with ANY web-archive.txt-publishing archive, not just other rustyweb instances. rustyweb keeps its richer NATIVE JSON API (task .2) for rustyweb-to-rustyweb specifics (live counts, capabilities, resolve); web-archive.txt is the interop lingua franca layered over it. NB: scope.authority / scope.coverage / scope.crawl modalities overlap the finding-aid provenance epic (rustyweb-findingaid) -- the descriptor is a natural machine-readable EXPORT of that curatorial metadata, so design the two together.

THREE LAYERS on top:
1. Read-only JSON API -- beyond /api/search: a NATIVE instance descriptor (name, version, collection/crawl counts, capabilities, instance base), /api/collections, /api/collections/{id}, /api/crawls/{id}, and a URL-resolution endpoint /api/resolve?url= -> [{crawl_id, ts, collection}] (page-level, index-backed). Each API result carries its persistent memento URL + the instance base. (The standard cross-archive identity doc is web-archive.txt, task .9; this native JSON is the richer rustyweb-to-rustyweb surface.)
2. Memento (RFC 7089) -- TimeMap + TimeGate + Memento-Datetime/Link headers, built on /api/resolve. Makes rustyweb a first-class Memento server so existing aggregators (Time Travel, MemGator) federate rustyweb instances at the URL level for free; these endpoints are ALSO advertised in web-archive.txt api.memento (task .9). Honest limitation: rustyweb indexes PAGES (HTML/PDF), not every subresource, so TimeMaps are page-level.
3. Federation -- an instance is configured with peer base URLs; it discovers each peer by fetching the peer's /.well-known/web-archive.txt (identity, scope, api endpoints), then does live FAN-OUT search: query self + peers concurrently (reuse the ureq client + retry/backoff + timeouts; degrade gracefully when a peer is down), merge + dedup + ATTRIBUTE each result to its origin instance so links open the peer's persistent replay URL. (Alternative considered: harvest peer catalogs into a local aggregate index -- scalable + resilient but stale/heavier; fan-out chosen for the no-central-service, self-host ethos.)

SYNERGY with cross-WACZ replay (rustyweb-cross-wacz-replay-dk4): dk4's leading approach is exactly a GET /api/resolve?url= lookup (landed on a page not in this crawl -> which other crawl has it -> re-launch). The resolve endpoint (task .3) is that building block; dk4 depends on it. dk4's temporal-coherence caution applies to choosing which crawl/ts to fall back to.

Decisions baked in (maintainer): URL shape = /crawl/{id}/{ts}/{url}; discovery/identity = web-archive.txt at /.well-known/ (adopt the spec, do not invent our own); federation = live fan-out; Memento = included. Task priorities + deps allow deferring Memento or federation. Read-only throughout; consider CORS for cross-instance browser calls and optional rate-limiting for a public API.

- /api/collections/{id} -> collection detail + members (crawl id/name/dates).

title: Memento (RFC 7089): TimeMap, TimeGate, Link/Memento-Datetime headers
description:
Expose rustyweb as a Memento server, built on the resolve endpoint (.3):
- TimeMap: GET /timemap/link/{url} (application/link-format) and /timemap/json/{url} -> all captures (URI-Ms = /crawl/{id}/{ts}/{url}) of a URL with their Memento-Datetimes.
- TimeGate: GET /timegate/{url} honoring Accept-Datetime -> 302 to the closest memento URI-M.
- Add Memento-Datetime + Link (rel=original/timemap/timegate/memento) headers on replay responses.
Enables existing aggregators (Time Travel, MemGator) to federate rustyweb instances at the URL level for free.

ADVERTISE these endpoints in web-archive.txt api.memento (task .9): timemap.endpoint + timegate.endpoint as URI templates with {url}/{datetime} placeholders (e.g. timegate = { endpoint = "https://host/timegate/{url}", access = "online" }), so the spec's validator/registry and any web-archive.txt-aware aggregator can find them without prior knowledge. The persistent replay URL maps to replay.rewritten (and a no-toolbar variant to replay.no_toolbar) in the same descriptor.

Honest limitation to document: page-level coverage only (rustyweb indexes pages, not every subresource). Temporal coherence: each URI-M is single-crawl-scoped and coherent. Files: server.rs (routes + headers), search.rs. Depends on .3.

title: Peer configuration for federation
description:
Let an instance be configured with a list of peer base URLs (read-only). Mechanism options to decide: a peers.json under <home> (portable with the home dir) vs a serve --peer flag vs both.

DISCOVER + VALIDATE each peer by fetching its /.well-known/web-archive.txt descriptor (the web-archive.txt spec, task .9) and parsing the TOML: archive.id + archive.name (identity/attribution label), archive.scope (domains / temporal coverage / collections -- lets fan-out skip peers whose scope cannot match a query), and the api.* / replay templates (how to query + how to build the peer's replay/memento URLs). Handle unreachable/incompatible/no-descriptor peers gracefully. Because web-archive.txt is a community spec, a peer need NOT be a rustyweb instance -- any archive publishing a descriptor with api.memento can be federated at the Memento level (task .8); rustyweb peers additionally expose the native /api/ (task .2) for the richer view, so prefer /.well-known/web-archive.txt for identity and fall back to / enrich with /api/ when the peer is rustyweb.

A minimal parser for the four web-archive.txt sections (version/archive/api/replay) is needed here on the CONSUME side; it is the mirror of the PUBLISH side in task .9 -- share a serde struct + a toml dep between them. - version: version = "0.1" (spec version), last_updated (date the descriptor/manifest last changed).
- archive: id (short slug -- config/serve flag), name (inline table, en + optional alt), established?, website (public base URL), email?.

title: Search/facet by source kind (local vs remote)
description:
Let users filter and facet search results by whether a crawl is stored locally or hosted remotely (a remote URL, or a streamed Browsertrix source). Complements the local/remote source pills added in rustyweb-15z.9 (PR #53) — the same distinction, now as a search dimension: e.g. "show only content I have a durable local copy of," or "only streamed crawls."

Design note / the wrinkle: source kind is a property of the crawl’s manifest Source (File vs Url/Browsertrix), and it is MUTABLE without re-indexing content — `index --download` turns a remote URL into a local File, and a Browsertrix source is remote. So an index-time Tantivy field would go stale until a reindex.

Two approaches:
- (a) Index a `source_kind` (local|remote) field/facet on each doc. Simple faceting, but a SCHEMA CHANGE (reindex) and it can drift from the manifest when a source’s kind changes; must be recomputed on every (re)index.
- (b) Derive from the manifest at query time (recommended). Low cardinality (two values) + the crawl→kind map is cheap to build from the manifest. A `source:local` / `source:remote` query alias expands to `crawl_id:(…)` over the matching crawls (mirrors the existing `crawl:` alias rewrite in server.rs), and the facet counts are computed from the manifest ∩ the result set. No reindex, always fresh.

Recommend (b). Surface it as a facet in the results sidebar (like site/year/type) and a `source:` filter. Files: search.rs (facet aggregation / alias), server.rs (query rewrite + facet UI), views.rs. Relates to the crawl/site/type faceting already present and to the source pills (rustyweb-15z.9).

title: Index extracted page text from Browsertrix pages.jsonl / extraPages.jsonl (fixes JS-rendered content being unsearchable)
description:
Index the extracted page `text` from Browsertrix pages.jsonl / extraPages.jsonl.

Root cause found while debugging a SUCHO search miss: searching the homepage term "Петиція" (on https://uinp.gov.ua/) returns nothing, even though it's clearly visible in replay. The term is JS-rendered, so it is NOT in the raw HTML response body (confirmed). Browsertrix captured the rendered text, but for this 2022-vintage crawl it wrote it into the WACZ's pages files, NOT as `urn:text:` WARC records:
- CDX has 30044 records and ZERO `urn:` records (no urn:text:).
- pages/pages.jsonl (seed pages) and pages/extraPages.jsonl (4150 pages here) each have a `text` field per entry.
- The homepage pages.jsonl entry has text (2708 chars) that DOES contain "Петиція".

rustyweb currently reads pages.jsonl only for seed-page metadata (url/title/ts -> seed_pages) and ignores the `text` field; it never reads extraPages.jsonl. Body text is taken from urn:text: (absent here) or scraped HTML (missing JS-rendered content). Result: rendered content is unsearchable and recall is badly degraded for Browsertrix crawls of this shape -- including the flagship SUCHO demo.

Fix: during indexing, also read the `text` (and title) from pages/pages.jsonl AND pages/extraPages.jsonl, and merge it into the per-URL page body -- treat it like Browsertrix rendered text (same role as the urn:text: path). Prefer rendered text (urn:text OR pages-jsonl text) over scraped HTML for the body; keep HTML title/description/lang where richer.

Considerations:
- Both index paths must do it: the default CDX-guided/streaming path (collect_page_records_via_cdx) does not currently read pages.jsonl at all for text; the full-scan path (index_wacz) doesn't either. The pages files are small zip entries -- cheap to read once during setup (the streaming setup already opens the ZIP central directory).
- Merge by URL into the existing MergedPage (add a source, e.g. jsonl_text, slotted with rendered_text). Decide precedence: urn:text: vs pages.jsonl text (they're the same kind of data; either is fine -- prefer whichever is present).
- Skip the header line ({format,id,title}) in each jsonl. Handle both pages.jsonl and extraPages.jsonl; tolerate absence (py-wacz and some WACZs have no text).
- Pages that exist only in extraPages.jsonl (not surfaced as a page today) should become searchable pages, tagged to the WACZ/collection like any other page. Watch doc counts (this could add many docs -- here ~4150/WACZ).
- Titles from pages.jsonl may be better than scraped ones; consider using them as a fallback.
- Timestamps: pages.jsonl has ts; use for the page if the HTML capture ts is missing (mirror the urn:text merge which only fills an empty ts).
- Add a regression test with a fixture WACZ that has pages.jsonl text but the term absent from HTML, asserting the term is searchable after indexing.

Impact: HIGH -- fixes a large class of "I can see it in replay but can't search it" misses on the SUCHO demo and directly improves the Browsertrix importer (15z) results, since those are exactly these WACZs. P1.

Relates to the Browsertrix importer epic (rustyweb-15z) and the urn:text: rendered-text handling already in index.rs (record_to_raw / index_merged).
close_reason: Implemented: read the text field from pages/pages.jsonl + pages/extraPages.jsonl and fold it into the per-URL page body (interchangeable with urn:text:), in both the CDX-guided and full-scan paths. Unit test (read_page_texts) + end-to-end test (term present only in pages.jsonl is searchable via the default path). title: Expose an MCP endpoint so agents can search & retrieve the archive
description:
Serve a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint from the rustyweb server so LLM agents (Claude, etc.) can discover and use a web archive as a tool — search full text, list collections/crawls, resolve a URL to its captures, and fetch a page's archived text/metadata — without scraping the HTML UI.

## Why
rustyweb already has the retrieval primitives (Tantivy full-text search, the collections/crawls model, CDX URL resolution). MCP is the emerging standard for handing those to agents. This turns the archive into a first-class research tool an agent can call, and dovetails with the read-only JSON API in the federation epic (rustyweb-federation-shwl.2/.3) — same data, agent-facing framing.

## Sketch (to be designed)
- Transport: MCP over HTTP (streamable HTTP / SSE) mounted on the existing axum server, e.g. under `/mcp`. Consider a Rust MCP server crate vs. a hand-rolled JSON-RPC handler; keep deps light (the project avoids heavy deps).
- Tools to expose (read-only first):
  - `search(query, limit, collection?)` → ranked hits (url, ts, crawl, snippet).
  - `list_collections()` / `get_collection(slug)` → finding-aid metadata.
  - `list_crawls(collection?)` / `get_crawl(id)` → crawl provenance.
  - `resolve_url(url)` → captures/timestamps for a URL (Memento-ish; overlaps shwl.3 `/api/resolve`).
  - `get_page(crawl, ts, url)` → archived text + headers/metadata (not raw replay bytes).
- Resources: optionally expose collections as MCP resources.
- Auth/safety: read-only; respect any access controls; bound result sizes; no replay-bytes firehose.

## Open questions
- Reuse the shwl.2 JSON API handlers under the hood (share a service layer) vs. a parallel implementation.
- Which Rust MCP library, if any, meets the light-deps bar.
- Whether to gate behind a `--mcp` serve flag or always-on.

Best built on top of the read-only JSON API (rustyweb-federation-shwl.2) so both share one query/service layer.

title: Use Browsertrix screenshot records as the preferred crawl thumbnail
description: Browsertrix crawls (when screenshots are enabled — common) store a rendered screenshot of each page in a screenshots WARC, surfaced in the CDX as: - urn:thumbnail: → a small, ready-made thumbnail (image/jpeg, ~20-30KB) - urn:view: → the full viewport screenshot (image/png, larger) keyed by the EXACT page URL. Verified in a real crawl: urn:thumbnail:https://lawfaremedia.github.io/jan6-doj-archive/ → image/jpeg 22854 bytes; urn:view:... → image/png 169525 bytes. Our thumbnail picker (thumbnail.rs generate()) ignores these entirely, and its tier-3 "largest on-site captured image" actively EXCLUDES them: it filters candidates by site_of(main_page_url) (registrable domain), and a urn:thumbnail:/urn:view: URL does not parse to that host, so it never matches. Result: JS-rendered pages (SPAs, github.io, SUCHO, etc.) with no og:image and no raw-HTML get NO thumbnail even though a perfect screenshot exists in the WACZ. Fix — add a TIER-0 (highest priority) in generate(), before og:image: 1. find_image_record(cdx, &format!("urn:thumbnail:{main_page_url}")) — use it if present (already thumbnail-sized JPEG; skip the size window / on-site checks, it is purpose-built). 2. else find_image_record(cdx, &format!("urn:view:{main_page_url}")) — the full screenshot; downscale via the existing write_thumbnail (400px). Fetch the record bytes with the existing fetch_record_bytes (works local + streaming), then write_thumbnail as today. Respect a pinned thumbnail (curator override) first, as now. Notes: - Broadly beneficial: this becomes the primary thumbnail source for Browsertrix-crawled content (the importer’s bread and butter) and fixes the "no image" cases we saw on SUCHO/reallifemag-style JS pages. - Regenerated on (re)index like other thumbnails, so a reindex picks it up. - main_page_url must match the screenshot record’s page URL exactly (datapackage mainPageUrl / first seed); handle a trailing-slash mismatch defensively. - Relates to the existing thumbnail heuristic (three-tier), the per-page og:image gallery idea (rustyweb-crawl-ogimage-gallery-vi3n), and thumb GC (rustyweb-thumb-gc-2x5c). Files: thumbnail.rs (generate + a screenshot lookup helper), maybe a small is_screenshot_url helper; DESIGN "Representative-image thumbnails" section. Test: a fixture WACZ with a urn:thumbnail record → generate() picks it.

title: Production deployment in the cloud (reverse-proxy fronted)
description:
Set up a production deployment of rustyweb in the cloud, fronted by a modern reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy, or similar) for TLS and public-facing concerns. rustyweb is a single self-contained binary that serves HTTP via axum (default 127.0.0.1:8080); the deployment wraps that for real-world hosting while keeping the 'range' ethos: the same setup should suit a small VPS and scale up toward an institutional host.

Goal: a documented, reproducible way to run rustyweb publicly (TLS, a domain, restart-on-failure) with the reverse proxy handling the edge and rustyweb serving search + WACZ bytes.

rustyweb-specific considerations:
- BYTE-RANGE PASSTHROUGH is critical: replay is WACZ-direct — the browser reads GET /files/{id} with HTTP Range requests via wabac.js. The proxy must pass Range/Accept-Ranges/Content-Range through untouched and not buffer whole (multi-GB) WACZ responses (e.g. nginx: proxy_buffering off / proxy_max_temp_file_size 0, or use a proxy that streams ranges well). Verify large-file range serving end to end through the proxy.
- TLS termination at the proxy (Let's Encrypt). Caddy does this automatically; nginx needs certbot. Pick one.
- Run rustyweb bound to localhost, as a non-root user, index opened read-only (serve already opens read-only); only the proxy is public.
- Persistent storage for <home> (archive/ + index/). Streaming remote WACZs keeps disk small (index only); a local archive needs a durable volume. Decide the storage model per target.
- Compression is already done in-process (tower-http); avoid double-compressing at the proxy. Don't gzip byte-range responses.
- CORS: same-origin replay (WACZ served by rustyweb) needs none; replaying a *remote* WACZ needs that remote host's CORS — document the distinction.
- Health/readiness endpoint for the proxy / orchestrator (likely need to add a lightweight /health route — none today).
- Observability: tracing logs to stdout/journald; access logs at the proxy.

Deployment shapes to evaluate (pick 1-2):
- Container: single static binary -> tiny distroless/scratch OCI image; run on a VM, Fly.io, Cloud Run, ECS, etc. Assets are embedded at build time, so the image is self-contained.
- VM + systemd: a systemd unit for rustyweb + the proxy config on a VPS/EC2/droplet.

Open decisions: which reverse proxy (Caddy = simplest TLS; nginx = ubiquitous), which cloud target (VM vs managed container platform), container vs systemd, and where <home> lives (ephemeral + stream-only, or a persistent volume).

Deliverables (candidate child tasks): reverse-proxy config with verified range passthrough (nginx + Caddy examples); Dockerfile / OCI image (distroless); systemd unit + VM deploy guide; /health endpoint; a Deployment section in README/DESIGN. Relates to the scale-footprint direction (rustyweb-scale-footprint-qw5) and to streaming (remote-only deploys need little disk).

title: Make reindex resilient to transient remote-fetch failures
description:
`rustyweb reindex` currently fails fast: it drops the old full-text index up front, then re-indexes every registered source, and the first error (e.g. a transient network read on a remote WACZ) aborts the whole run — leaving the index partially rebuilt. With a collection of remote WACZs (e.g. the `sul` Stanford stacks collection) a single flaky fetch means the entire reindex is lost and must be restarted from scratch (re-fetching everything, ~20+ min), where it may fail again.

This bit us during the faceting work: reindex died at 9/19 on a transient read of a remote WACZ, and the Browsertrix collections (later in the manifest) never got indexed.

Desired behavior: a transient remote-fetch failure should be treated like a missing local file already is — logged as a warning and skipped, preserving the WACZ's manifest entry — so the rest of the reindex completes. At the end, print a summary of any skipped sources and exit non-zero (so cron/CI notices) while still leaving a usable, mostly-complete index.

Scope / considerations:
- Distinguish transient/remote-fetch errors (skip + warn) from programmer/logic errors (still fail). Start by making remote fetch/parse failures non-fatal; keep local validation (path outside archive, non-.wacz) fail-fast as today.
- Consider ret/retries with backoff for remote fetches before giving up on one.
- Consider not dropping the old index until the rebuild succeeds, or building into a temp dir and swapping — so a failed reindex doesn't destroy a working index. (Bigger change; could be a follow-up.)
- Report a clear end-of-run summary: N indexed, M skipped (with reasons).
- Tests: a source that errors is skipped and the run completes over the rest.

Relates to the remote-WACZ collections use case and the Browsertrix importer epic (rustyweb-15z), which will add more remote sources.
close_reason: Both remaining follow-ups delivered: reindex skip-on-failure (with non-zero exit + summary) and per-host concurrency cap (MAX_CONCURRENCY=64).

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Scope (maintainer concern): broaden this beyond "retry transient failures" to robust AND POLITE remote fetching. Now that CDX-guided record fetch is concurrent (r0n.7, default --concurrency 16), a single WACZ's requests all hit ONE host, so we can overload a small/self-hosted server or get IP-blocked when the target isn't a big object store like S3.

Key measure: honor HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) and 503 + the Retry-After header with exponential backoff, for both the range fetches (http_range::HttpFetch) and the whole-file downloads. This is simultaneously resilience (recover from transient/overload errors, per this task's original intent) AND politeness (back off when a host pushes back, instead of hammering -> far less likely to get blocked).

Also consider:
- A per-host rate and/or concurrency cap (proactive politeness), separate from the raw --concurrency worker count.
- Revisiting the default --concurrency: 16 is tuned for object stores; a lower default (or a "be gentle" mode) may be safer when pointing rustyweb at arbitrary hosts, which matters for the self-serve / adoption story.
- Retry with jittered backoff on transient network errors, and a bounded retry budget, so a long ingest survives blips without giving up or busy-looping.

Ties to the streaming epic (r0n) and the shareable/self-serve goal (others will point rustyweb at arbitrary hosts, not just S3).
